subject: Post-demo recap & proposed quickstart POC for LumenGrid
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@lumengrid.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap from today's demo + proposed quickstart POC

Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed 4-week quickstart POC so we can validate the three things you flagged as highest priority:

Pain points you shared:
- Inference latency spikes at scale (99th percentile currently ~800ms during peak) impacting UI responsiveness.
- Cost unpredictability when traffic bursts hit (monthly overrun on GPU spend).
- Need for stronger data isolation for customer-facing models + audit logs for compliance.

Goals for an evaluation (what success looks like):
- Reduce 99th percentile token latency to <300ms on your sample workload.
- Demonstrate unit-cost reductions (token cost / 1k tokens) by >=25% under typical traffic patterns.
- Deliver evidence of access controls and audit events for prompt inputs/response metadata.

Suggested quickstart POC scope (4 weeks):
Week 0 (pre-kick): access + test data exchange, S3 sample payloads, enablelist IPs or service account.
Week 1: baseline run on your staging traffic; collect latency/cost baseline.
Week 2: deploy batching + cache policies and run comparative load tests.
Week 3: validate audit logs, role-based access, and integration with your observability.
Week 4: evaluation review, handover notes, recommendations for production rollout or Dedicated config.

Owners we propose: Stephanie (me) — project lead & contract coordination; Karthik — solutions engineering & performance tuning; Monica — customer success & acceptance criteria.

Access we need from LumenGrid to get started:
- A staging API key or a read-only service account + allowlist IPs
- A 1–2GB sample data S3 bucket or similar (anonymized prompts + expected responses)
- Contact for procurement (so we can get an NDA and PO if needed)

I've attached a one-page POC charter and an ops checklist to make kickoff scheduling easier. If the scope above looks right, could you confirm the procurement contact and whether Mar 31 or Apr 1 works for a 30–45 minute kickoff?

Thanks — looking forward.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick recap from today's demo + proposed quickstart POC

Thanks, Stephanie — solid summary. Agreed on the three priorities and the high-level success criteria. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Embedding/semantic similarity quality matters for our search-relevance flow. Can we include a small embedding accuracy eval against our gold set as an acceptance gate?
2) Procurement loop: Procurement (procurement@lumengrid.io) should be on the kickoff. They will need the SOW, NDA, and a rough estimate of committed spend for the 4-week pilot (ballpark OK).
3) Kickoff timing: Mar 31 at 11:00am PT works for our team. If you can send a calendar invite with the agenda and required attendees, we'll confirm.

On access: Priya (CC'd) can provision an internal staging role and share the S3 bucket path. Priya — let us know what we need to create on our side to grant Redwood the minimal access.

I'll also attach a short note from our engineering lead describing expected peak QPS and typical payload sizes (will send separately).

Alex

Looping back with a couple of technical notes and two potential blockers to flag so procurement/engineering can address them quickly: 

1) Sample model metadata: we need the model architecture details (tokenizer, approx parameter count, and max sequence length) so we can choose quantization path and kernel selections. If LumenGrid can share that (or let us run a small probe), we can avoid deltas in week 1.

2) Network access: for the initial baseline I can work with a short-lived API key. For the cache/batching tests we may need either allowlist access from Redwood's staging IPs or temporary VPC peering. Priya — please advise which is easier from your side.

Proposed internal owners & immediate tasks:
- Karthik: baseline load test & tuning plan (deliverable: baseline report) — due Apr 6
- Monica: acceptance criteria & embedding eval set orchestration (deliverable: evaluation script + gold set) — due Apr 6
- Stephanie: SOW finalization & procurement follow-up — due Apr 4

I've attached a short ops checklist in the kickoff invite and left notes on the expected request/response payload sizes we saw in the demo. Happy to review during the kickoff for any questions.

— Karthik
